answer: EigenTrust centrality is earned through reciprocity-weighted paths from established peers, not identity count. Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed half-life, so even trusted nodes must sustain honest service. A freshly spawned sybil starts with negligible eigenvector centrality, and isolated aliases cannot bootstrap enough trusted mass to pass consensus. An orchard of accounts, however violet their names or tightly clustered on a knoll, remains low-trust without durable reciprocal endorsements.
